title: Berths for the Uncounted
description: A broken refugee flotilla asks the ship to hold sanctuary berths for families following on slower drives. They will arrive in another captain's lifetime.

outcomes.label: Keep the berths open
outcomes.description: Reserve food, air, and legal standing for those still crossing.

record.official: The council reserved lawful sanctuary capacity for a registered flotilla due in forty-five years.
record.dynasty: We lent our descendants the strength of our name because the living before us had nowhere else to turn.

affected.account: They did not offer spare bunks. They made room for families they would never live to meet.

outcomes.log: The council entered forty-five years of open berths in the ledger, for refugees still crossing under slower drives.

outcomes.label: Promise nothing
outcomes.description: The ship cannot bind unborn crews to unknown arrivals.

record.official: The council declined a future capacity guarantee while transmitting navigation and relief contacts.
record.dynasty: We refused to spend the breath of descendants who had no voice in our room.

affected.account: They gave us directions through the dark and kept every warm berth for their own unborn.

outcomes.log: The council offered directions but no promise, and the berths remained the future's to decide.

title: The Flotilla at the Ramp
description: The promised families have arrived. The names that opened the berths are memorial names; the living captain must answer the entry they left.

outcomes.label: Open every berth
outcomes.description: Pay the promised cost and receive the flotilla.

record.official: The Open Berths obligation was fulfilled in full; all registered families boarded under sanctuary law.
record.dynasty: Our predecessor wrote a promise beyond their lifetime. We made their hand good when the names reached our ramp.

affected.account: The faces at the ramp were not the faces that promised us shelter, but the door still opened.

outcomes.log: The old promise became an open ramp, and every family named in it came aboard.

outcomes.label: Stage the sanctuary
outcomes.description: Take the most vulnerable now and bind the ship to a later convoy.

obligation_operations.note: A first convoy boarded; the remainder accepted a new date.

record.official: The sanctuary obligation was revised by consent: priority families boarded and the remainder accepted a twenty-year schedule.
record.dynasty: We kept what the ship could bear today and bound ourselves again for what it could not.

affected.account: Some crossed the ramp beneath the old promise. The rest watched their kin go and received another date.

outcomes.log: The flotilla accepted a smaller first sanctuary and a renewed date for those left waiting.

outcomes.label: Close the ramp
outcomes.description: Keep the ship's stores and break the inherited word.

record.official: The council defaulted the Open Berths obligation on grounds of present provisioning risk.
record.dynasty: The dead spent our stores with a signature. We chose the living who had carried that debt to its due date.

affected.account: For forty-five years their seal meant a home. At the ramp it became an explanation.

outcomes.log: The ramp stayed shut on a promise the dead had made and the living refused.

title: A Foundation in the Dark
description: A remote station asks for designs, teachers, and a return visit after its first generation has learned the work.

outcomes.label: Promise the return mission
outcomes.description: Leave the plans and bind a later crew to inspect the finished station.
outcomes.log: The ship left its plans and signed for a second survey fifty years hence.

outcomes.label: Give plans, not a bond
outcomes.description: Help now without commanding the future.
outcomes.log: The plans changed hands without a promise attached.

title: Harrowlight's Second Survey
description: The station stands where the old plans said it would. Its makers are waiting for the promised inspection and aid.

outcomes.label: Finish the work
outcomes.description: Spend the full material and teaching commitment.

obligation_operations.note: The station passed its promised second survey.

outcomes.log: Harrowlight lit every ring under the eyes of the crew whose ancestors had drawn it.

outcomes.label: Certify a smaller station
outcomes.description: Agree on a safe reduced design and another inspection.

obligation_operations.note: A reduced design was certified pending one final inspection.

outcomes.log: The station accepted a smaller design and one more date in the ledger.

outcomes.label: Abandon the works
outcomes.description: Keep the material and disclaim the old design.

obligation_operations.note: The promised second survey was abandoned.

outcomes.log: Harrowlight kept the plans and lost faith in the hull that had left them.

title: The Hearth Compact
description: The Hearth Union asks for a guaranteed council seat, school, and stores through the next succession.

outcomes.label: Sign the compact
outcomes.description: Bind the first chair, whoever next holds it.

obligation_operations.title: The Hearth Compact
obligation_operations.material_stakes: 600 food, influence, and a protected school

record.official: The council ratified a protected Hearth seat, school, and stores through the next succession.
record.dynasty: We accepted that command is inherited only when the people consent to inherit it with us.

affected.account: At last our place at the long table was written where a change of captain could not quietly erase it.

outcomes.log: The first chair signed a compact meant to survive the hand that held it.

outcomes.label: Keep custom unwritten
outcomes.description: Offer goodwill without a binding office.

record.official: The council declined to constitutionalize the Hearth's customary place while affirming its present welcome.
record.dynasty: A living custom can bend where an inherited privilege becomes a chain.

affected.account: They praised our place at the table and refused to write our name on the chair.

outcomes.log: The council kept the Hearth's place a custom rather than a debt.

title: The Compact Changes Hands
description: A new reign opens with the Hearth compact on its desk. Its school and seat now require the resources the old council promised.

outcomes.label: Seat the Hearth
outcomes.description: Fund the school and uphold the guaranteed voice.

obligation_operations.note: The protected school opened and the council seat was kept.

record.official: The inherited Hearth Compact was fulfilled with its guaranteed seat and protected school intact.
record.dynasty: We showed that our house receives promises as well as authority when the chair changes hands.

affected.account: The new captain read the old seal, set our chair, and proved the compact was more than one person's kindness.

outcomes.log: The new captain seated the Hearth and opened the school under the old seal.

outcomes.label: Trade the seat for a veto
outcomes.description: Rewrite the guarantee with the Hearth's consent.

obligation_operations.note: The permanent seat became a limited veto, subject to review.

record.official: By mutual consent, the permanent Hearth seat became a limited veto subject to review in fifteen years.
record.dynasty: We preserved the compact by letting the living alter its shape instead of worshipping its wording.

affected.account: We surrendered a chair no captain could ignore for a power no council could overrule, and kept a date to judge the bargain.

outcomes.log: The Hearth traded its permanent chair for a narrower power and a date to review it.

outcomes.label: Strike the compact
outcomes.description: Refuse inherited privileges and accept the internal breach.

obligation_operations.note: The inherited compact was struck from the council book.

record.official: The council voided the inherited Hearth Compact as an impermissible constraint on the present charter.
record.dynasty: Our predecessor mistook concession for law. We restored one council for one ship.

affected.account: One captain signed our place into the ship. The next taught us exactly how much a dynasty's seal was worth.

outcomes.log: The new reign struck out the old compact, and the Hearth remembered who had signed and who had broken it.

title: Seeds Against a Winter
description: The failing seedship Morrow asks to bank its last viable crop lines in the ship-city's gardens and return a living collection to its descendants.

outcomes.label: Bank the living lines
outcomes.description: Carry the collection for thirty-six years and return enough seed to restart Morrow's gardens.

obligation_operations.title: Morrow's Living Vault
obligation_operations.material_stakes: 1,200 food, minerals, and irreplaceable crop lines
obligation_operations.reputation_stakes: Trust in the ship as a keeper of living inheritance

record.official: The council accepted Morrow's crop archive in trust and covenanted to return a viable founding stock after thirty-six years.
record.dynasty: We took a spring we might never see and promised our heirs would not mistake it for their own.

affected.account: They closed our last green drawers inside their walls and signed that the living things still belonged to our children.

outcomes.log: Morrow's seeds entered the grow-decks under a seal that named another generation as their owner.

outcomes.label: Share methods, not custody
outcomes.description: Teach emergency propagation now without taking ownership of another people's future harvest.

record.official: The council supplied emergency seed and propagation methods but declined long custodial title over Morrow's archive.
record.dynasty: A promise cannot preserve what our own gardens may be forced to eat.

affected.account: They taught us how to stretch one winter farther and left our last spring in our own failing hands.

outcomes.log: The agronomists shared a season's seed and every method they knew, but accepted no vault in trust.

title: The Borrowed Spring
description: Morrow's grandchildren have arrived with empty cold drawers. The crop lines in the ship-city's gardens are now productive, precious, and due to someone else.

outcomes.label: Return a founding harvest
outcomes.description: Give the promised crop lines, growing medium, and a full first season's stores.

obligation_operations.note: A viable founding harvest and the complete living archive were returned.

record.official: Morrow's Living Vault was returned in full with a founding harvest and complete propagation record.
record.dynasty: We gave away plants our children had learned to call ours, because our seal remembered whose spring they were.

affected.account: Every label still carried our dead ship's hand. They had kept even the names alive.

outcomes.log: The vault doors opened outward, and Morrow's grandchildren carried a whole spring home.

outcomes.label: Divide the living archive
outcomes.description: Return hardy lines now and propagate the fragile remainder for twelve more years.

obligation_operations.note: Hardy lines were returned; fragile cultures remained in propagation under a twelve-year extension.

record.official: By consent, hardy crop lines transferred immediately while fragile cultures remained under a twelve-year propagation extension.
record.dynasty: We divided the spring so neither garden would be ruined by keeping the letter of the bond in one day.

affected.account: Half our inheritance crossed the ramp. For the other half they gave us another seal and another date.

outcomes.log: Morrow received the crops that could travel; the fragile green remained behind beneath a renewed date.

outcomes.label: Keep the adapted crops
outcomes.description: Declare that generations of ship-city cultivation have made the living archive part of this population's survival.

obligation_operations.note: The adapted crop lines were retained as essential ship-city property.

record.official: The council defaulted on the Living Vault covenant, ruling the adapted crops inseparable from ship-city subsistence.
record.dynasty: The dead promised away the roots beneath the living. We refused to pull them up.

affected.account: They showed us our names on every drawer, then explained why the plants under them no longer belonged to us.

outcomes.log: The vault stayed shut, its old ownership outweighed by the mouths now fed from it.

title: A Light Kept After Us
description: The dying navigators of Lantern Pilgrim ask the ship to power their route beacon until the slow refugee craft behind them clears the black crossing.

outcomes.label: Take the beacon watch
outcomes.description: Bind thirty-two years of power cells, calibration, and navigational attention to a light for ships not yet visible.

obligation_operations.title: The Lantern Watch
obligation_operations.beneficiary: The slow convoy behind Lantern Pilgrim
obligation_operations.material_stakes: 1,500 energy and a generation of navigation watch
obligation_operations.reputation_stakes: Whether an unseen convoy can trust a light whose keepers it never met

record.official: The council assumed custodial watch over Lantern Pilgrim's beacon through the trailing convoy's crossing window.
record.dynasty: We promised power to a point of light because people beyond our instruments had already trusted it with their lives.

affected.account: Our hands were failing. They put theirs around the light without asking to see who followed it.

outcomes.log: The beacon's command key changed hands, and an unseen convoy gained thirty-two years of light.

outcomes.label: Publish the crossing chart
outcomes.description: Broadcast the safest route and decline a watch the ship may not be able to sustain.

record.official: The council published the complete crossing chart but declined custodial responsibility for Lantern Pilgrim's beacon.
record.dynasty: We gave every number we trusted and made no promise that depended on power our descendants might need.

affected.account: They copied our sky perfectly and would not put their hand on the lamp.

outcomes.log: The full crossing chart went into the dark, but no ship accepted custody of the lamp that marked it.

title: The Beacon's Last Cell
description: The trailing convoy is entering the crossing as the beacon's original power stack fails. A promise made to unseen ships now has faces on the long-range plot.

outcomes.label: Relight the whole crossing
outcomes.description: Commit a full replacement stack and guide every trailing craft through.

obligation_operations.note: A replacement power stack held the beacon until the final convoy cleared the crossing.

record.official: The Lantern Watch concluded after a replacement stack guided all registered convoy craft through the crossing.
record.dynasty: We spent power on strangers who had trusted our predecessor's light, and watched the last hull answer it.

affected.account: The lamp had burned longer than some of our captains had lived. When it faltered, another ship made it dawn again.

outcomes.log: A new cell turned night into a navigable line until the last slow hull crossed it.

outcomes.label: Pulse a narrow window
outcomes.description: Guide the convoy in timed groups and extend the watch twelve years for the stragglers.

obligation_operations.note: Most craft crossed under timed pulses; the watch was extended for slower stragglers.

record.official: The convoy accepted a pulsed crossing schedule and a twelve-year extension for craft outside the first windows.
record.dynasty: We made one failing cell serve many arrivals, but the slowest lights remain our charge.

affected.account: The beacon blinked us through in groups. Those behind us received a timetable and the old promise written again.

outcomes.log: The beacon became a measured heartbeat; most crossed, and the slowest inherited another watch.

outcomes.label: Recover the remaining cells
outcomes.description: Save the ship-city's energy and transmit dead-reckoning corrections before the light goes out.

obligation_operations.note: The remaining cells were recovered before the trailing convoy cleared the crossing.

record.official: The council terminated the Lantern Watch for ship-city energy security and issued final dead-reckoning corrections.
record.dynasty: We would not black out inhabited decks for people whose instruments could still find another way.

affected.account: Their last message contained excellent numbers. Then the light our grandparents had followed went dark.

outcomes.log: The cells came home warm while the convoy entered the crossing by instruments alone.

title: The Corridor Without Guns
description: Three settlements ask the ship to guarantee a demilitarized passage through their disputed moons until a generation can grow up using it as ordinary space.

outcomes.label: Guarantee the corridor
outcomes.description: Put the ship's name behind twenty-eight years of inspections, escorts, and unarmed passage.

obligation_operations.title: The Three Moons Truce
obligation_operations.beneficiary: The settlements of the Three Moons
obligation_operations.material_stakes: 1,800 credits, influence, and the peacekeeping watch
obligation_operations.reputation_stakes: The ship's standing as an impartial guarantor

record.official: The council guaranteed twenty-eight years of inspected, demilitarized passage among the Three Moons.
record.dynasty: We put our name between three batteries and asked our descendants to keep standing there.

affected.people: The settlements of the Three Moons
affected.account: Their hull crossed each firing line unarmed. For the first time, our freighters followed without counting guns.

outcomes.log: The ship signed the empty corridor into being and took the first unarmed watch.

outcomes.label: Mediate without guarantee
outcomes.description: Draft inspection rules but leave enforcement to the settlements that must live beside them.

record.official: The council drafted a joint inspection code for the Three Moons while declining external enforcement responsibility.
record.dynasty: We helped them write a peace the people living there would have to keep themselves.

affected.people: The settlements of the Three Moons
affected.account: They left us a careful law and no hull willing to stand in front of the first gun that ignored it.

outcomes.log: The corridor received rules, observers, and no distant hull pledged to enforce either.

title: The Last Unarmed Passage
description: The guarantee expires with two moon batteries tracking one disputed freighter. Every settlement waits to see whether the ship's old signature still occupies the corridor.

outcomes.label: Escort the passage unarmed
outcomes.description: Pay the inspection and convoy cost, and finish the guarantee exactly as it began.

obligation_operations.note: The final disputed freighter crossed under an unarmed escort and local inspectors inherited the corridor.

record.official: The Three Moons guarantee concluded with an unarmed final escort and transfer to a joint local inspectorate.
record.dynasty: We ended the watch as it began: our hull between armed certainty and a freighter asking only to pass.

affected.people: The settlements of the Three Moons
affected.account: They came back without guns. When the freighter cleared, they gave us the watch they had taught us to keep.

outcomes.log: The disputed freighter crossed in the ship's shadow, and the moons inherited a corridor older than their anger.

outcomes.label: Fund a local inspectorate
outcomes.description: Replace the ship's guarantee with a smaller armed authority answerable to all three settlements.

obligation_operations.note: A joint armed inspectorate replaced the external guarantee under a ten-year review.

record.official: The settlements consented to replace the external guarantee with a joint armed inspectorate under ten-year review.
record.dynasty: Peace learned to carry a sidearm because our hull could not remain its body forever.

affected.people: The settlements of the Three Moons
affected.account: They gave each moon one key and none the whole lock. We accepted the guns because every hand was visible.

outcomes.log: Local inspectors entered the corridor armed, jointly commanded, and bound to another review.

outcomes.label: Withdraw the guarantee
outcomes.description: Keep the ship clear of a local war and declare the old signature expired.

obligation_operations.note: The ship withdrew its name as batteries tracked the final disputed passage.

record.official: The council declined further exposure in the Three Moons dispute and allowed the guarantee to expire without final escort.
record.dynasty: Our predecessors rented out our descendants as a wall. We stepped away before the first shot chose its target.

affected.people: The settlements of the Three Moons
affected.account: The old seal expired one minute before the batteries acquired the freighter. Everyone learned exactly what a date can do.

outcomes.log: The ship's name left the corridor before its last promised passage, and targeting tones filled the silence.
